title: Kubernetes will finally make sense after this video

idea.title: Kubernetes will finally make sense after this video
idea.aha: Kubernetes is not a launcher, it's a set of loops that keep comparing what you asked for with what exists and fixing the difference.
idea.pain: You kill a pod to fix it and it instantly comes back, and you have no idea who brought it back or why.
didntKnow: kubectl apply doesn't start anything: it just writes your YAML into a database (etcd)
The scheduler's whole job is writing a node name into one field of the pod
Every component only talks to the API server; they never talk to each other directly
A Service usually isn't a running proxy: kube-proxy writes kernel packet rules (iptables/IPVS) on every node
Deleting a pod owned by a Deployment is a bug report to a loop, which immediately 'fixes' it
idea.visual: A WANT column and a HAVE column with a diff arrow; each controller is a small box running the same loop: read, compare, act
idea.device: Reconcile loop stamp: WANT 3 / HAVE 2 / ACT +1, reappearing for each component
idea.why: Most-used, least-understood infra tool; 'finally make sense' format proven at 150k+ on this niche
